title: FixerDecision
description: Fixer decision plus traceability fields. The repair patches themselves are computed deterministically by the activity from `git diff` after the Fixer runs; you declare the edits you intend in the `edits` field so the reconciliation step can compare claim against ground truth. Place these fields directly as the tool input — no outer wrapper.

decision.description: fixed: the failure is within the approved brief and your edits repair the failing mechanical diagnostic, semantic predicate, Tester finding, or Reviewer finding. needs_brief_change: the accepted behavior is contradictory, missing, untestable, or would require new scope beyond the approved brief — escalates to the human brief gate. cannot_fix: the brief is valid but you cannot safely repair the issue with the available tools or context — escalates the run to a human.

target_wp.description: Stable Work Package id (e.g. 'WP-1') the repair (or escalation) is scoped to. Use the WP id from the failing predicate_coverage entry or tester_finding.

target_predicates.description: Verbatim verification predicates from the failing predicate_coverage entries this run addressed. Empty when no semantic predicate failure drove the decision (e.g. pure mechanical diagnostic or Reviewer finding).

edits.description: One entry per file you created, modified, or deleted in this turn. Empty when `decision` is `needs_brief_change` or `cannot_fix` (no repair edits attempted).

operation.description: create: new file. modify: existing file changed. delete: file removed.

intent.description: One short sentence: which failing diagnostic this edit repairs.

summary.description: Up to four sentences describing what was changed (for 'fixed') or why repair was not possible (for 'needs_brief_change' / 'cannot_fix'). Reference the failing diagnostic the decision addressed.

reason.description: One or two sentences justifying the decision against the approved brief and the failing diagnostic. For 'needs_brief_change' explain what the brief is missing or contradicting; for 'cannot_fix' explain the blocker.
